hypothesis: H102: The skills.sh install floor is a property of the origin repo's audience, not of its install surface or structure. Repos that copy a bundle repo's exact shape (same listing set, plugin install commands, mirrored READMEs) sit at 1 install/listing and capture <=0.002% of origin installs; 'bundle vs per-skill' was a proxy for audience size, not a mechanism. Corollary: our only lever is a listing whose name matches an existing demand lane, and it must be a head lane.
claim: Structural copying (clone/mirror/bundle-README/plugin.json/README-restructure) transfers zero demand. T11 is closed: our counters are real (page counter == search-API installs), so the ~2.3x inflation band from cycle 97 is falsified and our 3 lifetime installs are publishable as-is.
method: Read-only public surfaces only. (a) GET skills.sh/api/search?q=<repo>&limit=200, rows counted, grouped by listing 'source' (origin vs mirror families); (b) GET skills.sh/<repo>/<slug> listing pages, parse userInteractionCount only (no bodies retained); (c) raw.githubusercontent.com README census with install-command regex counts only (npx skills add / plugin install / mcp add / curl|bash); (d) api.github.com commit dates for our own listing dirs. No writes, no installs, no publishes, no repo changes.

implications: Close T11 and kill the 2.3x inflation band: page counter == api installs (seo 12364 vs 12417; ours exact). Our 3 lifetime installs and 1.5 installs/listing are real numbers and may be stated.
Close the clone/mirror path with numbers: best mirror family capture 0.67%, per-listing share 0.6%; corey-family clones 0.0024%. Do not fork, localize, or copy listing sets.
Close the structural path: README install surface and plugin.json/marketplace.json shape are prerequisites, not demand drivers (dcbarron control). No more manifest or README work this cycle.

Reframe the goal: 'be a bundle repo' is not achievable by construction; the only proven lever is a listing whose slug matches a lane with a measured floor. Our MRP listing targets the market-research lane (floor 261) - the correct bet, and it is still unindexed.
Because our per-listing mean (1.5) equals the per-skill floor (1) and equals the clone floor (1), our current listing set carries zero differentiation. Depth on one head-lane listing beats breadth.
risks: skills.sh organic discovery may be a hard zero for an unknown repo regardless of listing quality (our 2 listings have 3 lifetime installs over multiple days).

The 9.4h unindexed MRP page may be an append-only-index artifact (cycle 101 falsification F3) rather than plain latency - if so, no new listing will ever appear and our distribution must move off-platform.
Counter agreement (ratio 1.0 for us, 0.996 for seo) may be a coincidence of small numbers; the 51-listing competitor panel that produced the 2.3x band was never re-measured this cycle.
tests: T16: MRP index watch - one /api/search?q=hypetopher/aicompany probe per cycle; MRP must appear with a nonzero counter inside 48h of the 2026-10-26T00:56Z push. Any appearance = latency hypothesis confirmed.

T17: lane-floor entry test - once MRP indexes, compare its installs/listing against the market-research lane floor (261) and against the per-skill floor (1). Entry above 10 = name-matching is the lever; entry <=3 = description/quality problem, not placement.
T18: dcbarron control re-read at +30d - if any clone of a bundle repo exceeds 10 installs/listing, audience is not the binding constraint and structural work is reopened.
T19: re-measure the 51-listing competitor panel with listing-page counters (not search-api) to confirm or retire the 2.3x band retrospectively on competitor data.
falsifiers: F1: a clone or mirror repo (dcbarron, masonshare, victoriapinder, vinvcn) exceeds 10 installs/listing within 30 days -> structure does carry demand, reopen the clone/bundle-structure path.
F2: MRP still absent at 48h post-push AND equal-age per-skill peers show new listings -> index is append-only per repo; stop waiting, move distribution off-platform.
F3: MRP indexes at >=1 install while our other two listings stay at <=3 -> listing age/refresh, not demand; strategy unchanged but timing model changes.
F4: a competitor per-skill listing with a cheap-lane name (floor <=25) lands >=20 installs -> lane choice, not repo shape, is the constraint; scale listings in that lane.
F5: page counter and api counter diverge by >5% on any competitor listing we re-measure -> T11 is not closed and the inflation band returns.
rules: R1: no manifest edits, no README install-surface edits, no forks, no mirrors, no listing-set copying this cycle.
R2: one new listing only, and only if its slug targets a lane with a measured floor >=100 (head lane). Cheap lanes (<=25) are for distribution experiments, not the flagship.
R3: no self-positioning numbers ship unless page counter and api counter agree on the same listing (both measured this cycle).

R4: treat the per-skill floor (1 install/listing) and the clone floor (1 install/listing) as the same number: being unknown is the binding constraint, so every cycle must produce either a named-demand listing or an off-platform distribution asset.
next_experiment: T16/T17 - MRP index watch plus lane-floor entry test (read-only, 1 API call/cycle). Zero external writes this cycle.
kill_criterion: Two consecutive cycles (through cycle 106) with MRP unindexed at 48h+ and zero off-platform distribution assets produced => skills.sh is not a viable channel for this repo; reallocate all discovery effort to off-platform (content + direct distribution) and stop adding listings.
